parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService works as an application-layer use-case service. It loads aggregates through injected repository ports (ProductRepository, OrderRepository), calls domain behaviour (Product.reserve, Product.canReserve, Product.consumeReserved, Product.release, Order.advanceTo, Order.cancel), coordinates work across the Order and Product aggregates, and saves the results through the ports. It contains no persistence code (no SQL, files or storage details), no transport or framework logic (no HTTP, request/response handling or status codes), and no presentation code. Its validation checks request input (required ids, positive integer quantities, known state filter). Checking every item before reserving any stock is use-case coordination. Order-state rules and stock rules stay inside the domain entities. A few borderline points remain: merging duplicate line items, the ALL_STATES filter check, and generating ids and timestamps with randomUUID and new Date. These could arguably move into domain factories, but they are normal for an application service and do not belong to another layer kind.
